messages:
From: Samantha Diaz <samantha@heathera.io>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 14:05:12 -0700
Subject: Production: sudden 5xx spike + latency — help needed

Lukas,

We started seeing elevated 5xx responses and token-level latency for several of our customer-facing endpoints around 13:50 PDT. Our telemetry shows a sustained rate limit rejections cluster and increased tail latency that coincides with a high-volume batch job. This is affecting ~15% of active sessions and causing timeouts in our mobile app.

I've attached a small set of sanitized logs (svc-logs-2028-07-28.zip) and a short capture of the call traces. Can Redwood confirm whether a policy change or quota update has rolled out?

We're on the hosted API (account ID: HTH-982). This is impacting our paid customers — would appreciate an urgent triage.

Thanks,
Samantha Diaz
Head of Site Reliability, Heathera Health

Quick update from infra triage (summary):
- Observed behavior: sudden increase in 429/503-level rejections and token-level tail latency for tenant HTH-982 starting 2028-07-28T20:47:00Z.
- Root cause: a mis-deployed burst/quota corridor change (config commit c7d4f8) introduced a narrower burst corridor window for hosted tenants sharing the shared-gpu pool. The new window overlapped with the tenant's steady-state pacing window which caused K/V cache pressure and request suppression for multi-shot generation patterns.
- Evidence: matching correlating logs (rate_limit.rejects and quota.window_hits) for HTH-982, and a deployment record showing the change at 2028-07-27 15:45 UTC.

Temporary mitigations we can apply immediately (recommended order):
1) Increase burst corridor allowances for HTH-982 to previous profile (revert corridor bounds) — low risk, immediate relief.
2) Route heavy generation traffic for HTH-982 to a dedicated pool (if available) for the next 2 hours.
3) Pin to a lower-latency model variant for high-concurrency routes (reduces KV pressure).

I attached a short proposal with the parameter changes and estimated cost delta. If we get exec signoff, infra can make the corridor change now and monitor.

Attachments: quota-adjustment-proposal.pdf

- Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Production: sudden 5xx spike + latency — help needed

Samantha — quick update from our side: we identified a narrow burst corridor window that inadvertently suppressed Heathera traffic during overlapping workloads. With Neha's approval we applied a temporary corridor increase and pinned a subset of heavy-generation routes to a dedicated path.

What we changed (temporary):
- Restored previous burst corridor bounds for HTH-982 at 2028-07-28T22:58:00Z (UTC).
- Enabled short-term routing of high-concurrency endpoints to a dedicated pool.

What to expect: latency and 5xx counts should reduce within the next 3–10 minutes; we'll monitor token-level rejects and reconnect logic. We'll keep the temporary measures for up to 3 hours while we complete a rollback plan and a formal postmortem.

Karthik attached a short parameter delta and cost estimate (quota-adjustment-proposal.pdf).

Can you confirm whether you see improvement on your side? If so we'll document and close the incident.

Thanks for flagging this so quickly — we'll follow up with a formal timeline and RCA.

— Lukas
